messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 

The failing test case `testDigitLimitConstructor` verifies that constructing a fraction from a double value close to a simple fraction with a max denominator doesn't throw an overflow exception:
```java
assertFraction(1, 2, new BigFraction(0.5000000001, 10));
```
This triggers the constructor `BigFraction(double value, int maxDenominator)` that internally calls `BigFraction(double value, double epsilon, int maxDenominator, int maxIterations)`.

From the retrieved source code snippet of `BigFraction(double value, double epsilon, int maxDenominator, int maxIterations)`:

- The method uses a continued fraction algorithm to approximate the double value as a fraction with numerator and denominator under certain limits (maxDenominator, maxIterations).
- It tracks intermediate numerator and denominator values (p2, q2) and checks for overflow against a `long overflow = Integer.MAX_VALUE`.
- If either p2 or q2 exceeds `overflow`, it throws a `FractionConversionException`.
- The relevant area is around lines 303-306:
  ```java
  if ((p2 > overflow) || (q2 > overflow)) {
      // in maxDenominator mode, if the last fraction was very close to the actual value
      // q2 may overflow in the next iteration; in this case return the last one.
      throw new FractionConversionException(value, p2, q2);
  }
  ```
- The comment hints that in some cases where the value is very close to a simple fraction but q2 overflows, the exception is thrown instead of returning the last good fraction.
- This matches the symptom of the bug report: "An overflow exception is thrown when a Fraction is initialized with a maxDenominator from a double very close to a simple fraction."
- The test uses as input 0.5000000001 which is very close to 1/2 but triggers the exception instead of returning 1/2 as expected.
- The problem is that the constructor throws an exception instead of falling back to return the previous convergent (last good fraction approximation).
- This points to an issue in the overflow detection and handling in this method `BigFraction(double, double, int, int)` where the last fraction should be returned rather than throwing.

In conclusion, the bug occurs due to overflow checks in the fraction construction algorithm that do not gracefully handle the case where the fraction is very close to a simple fraction but causes intermediate numerator/denominator to exceed `Integer.MAX_VALUE`. Instead of returning the last valid fraction, an exception is thrown improperly.

Recent bug reports about polynomial splines and event handlers are unrelated to the fraction conversion code and can be ignored.

The main fault lies in the overflow handling logic inside `BigFraction.BigFraction(double, double, int, int)`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
